records.label: Pedigree with two sisters with recurrent hydatidiform moles
quotes: We first focused on a pedigree in which two sisters were diagnosed with recurrent hydatidiform moles in December 2018. After genetic analysis, two novel mutations in MEI1 were identified.

records.label: Seven patients from six families with embryonic arrest/recurrent implantation failure
quotes: We then expanded the mutational screening to patients with the phenotype of embryonic arrest, recurrent implantation failure, and recurrent pregnancy loss, and found another three novel MEI1 mutations in seven new patients from six families recruited from December 2018 to May 2020.
Apart from recurrent hydatidiform moles, biallelic mutations in MEI1 were also associated with early embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure.

records.segregation: each variant inherited from a heterozygous parent
quotes: This study presents a case of a female infertile patient suffering from embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure.

We identified two novel pathogenic frameshift variants in the MEI1 gene (NM_152513.3, c.3002delC, c.2264_2268 + 11delGTGAGGTATGGACCAC) in the proband. These two variants were inherited from her heterozygous parents, consistent with autosomal recessive genetic transmission.
Notably, two Day 3 embryos and two Day 6 blastocysts were all aneuploid, with numerous monosomy and trisomy events.

records.segregation: Validated by Sanger sequencing in proband and family members; sister with normal fertility
quotes: The proband from family 1 (F1_II:4) carried compound heterozygous variants: c.622T > C (p.Ser208Pro) and c.2647 C > T (p.Arg883Ter) (Fig. 1B; Table 2).

The proband in family 1 (F1_II:4) was a 32-year-old woman with a 4-year history of primary infertility and no prior pregnancies. She had regular menstrual cycles and a normal ovarian reserve. Laparoscopy revealed a pelvic adhesion.

All 2PN-derived embryos from conventional IVF failed to form blastocysts, and no viable embryos were frozen or implanted. In contrast, two out of three 3PN/PPN-derived embryos from ICSI developed into late-stage blastocysts (Table 1).

records.label: F2_II:2
records.segregation: Validated by Sanger sequencing and qPCR in proband and family members
quotes: The proband from family 2 (F2_II:2) carried a compound heterozygous genotype for c.3037T > G (p.Trp1013Gly) and c.2546_3525del (EX21-31del) variants (Fig. 1B and S1; Table 2).
The proband in family 2 (F2_II:2) was a 35-year-old woman presented with an 8-year history of primary infertility. She had regular menstrual cycles and normal ovarian function.
All embryos failed to form blastocysts. Viable frozen embryos were implanted but failed to result in pregnancy.

These biallelic variants in MEI1 were associated with EEA and implantation failure.

records.label: Family with compound heterozygous MEI1 variants
quotes: We identified a novel homozygous variant and a compound heterozygous variant in MEI1 from two unrelated families.
These biallelic variants in MEI1 were associated with EEA and implantation failure.

notes.statement: Jiao et al. (2025) performed whole-exome sequencing in 20 women with a high rate of abnormal fertilization during ICSI and identified biallelic MEI1 variants in 2 of them.
quotes: Among these 20 patients, MEI1 variants were identified in two infertile women (F1_II:4 and F2_II:2).

notes.statement: In HEK293T cells, Jiao et al. (2025) found that the p.Arg883Ter variant increased MEI1 mRNA but reduced MEI1 protein. The p.Trp1013Gly variant increased protein levels, and the p.Ser208Pro variant and the exon 21-31 deletion did not change protein expression.
quotes: At the protein level, western blot analysis revealed that both p.Arg883Ter variants reduced MEI1 protein abundance (P = 0.031), consistent with nonsense-mediated decay of the truncated transcript
In contrast, p.Trp1013Gly increased protein levels (P = 0.016, Fig. 3, C-D). The p.Ser208Pro and E21_E31del variants did not alter protein expression

notes.statement: Jiao et al. (2025) analyzed embryos from one patient and found that all were triploid with excess maternal genome of meiotic origin; one arose from a meiosis II error and two from meiosis I errors. Two embryos also showed chromosomal aneuploidies.
quotes: However, qPCT confirmed that all embryos were triploid, with the majority of chromosomes originating from the maternal side (Fig. 4B).
we found that all three embryo samples exhibited BPH segments, indicating that they were triploid of meiotic origin
In the 3PN zygote, the region downstream of the centromere on chromosome 22 was classified as an SPH segment, suggesting that the triploidy resulted from meiosis II errors.

notes.statement: In RNA-seq of day-3 embryos from one patient, Jiao et al. (2025) found that downregulated genes were enriched for meiotic cell cycle, histone demethylase/deacetylase, and transcription coactivator functions. Maternal-effect genes, including FBXO43, OOEP, and WEE2, were dysregulated. The authors suggested that impaired zygotic genome activation may contribute to the phenotype.
quotes: GO enrichment analysis revealed that downregulated genes were strongly enriched in pathways related to meiotic cell cycle, beta-catenin binding, and epigenetic programming of transcription activation, including transcription coactivator activity, histone demethylase/deacetylase, and RNA polymerase mediated transcription
Importantly, maternal-effect genes exhibited significant dysregulation in the patient’s embryos, including FBXO43, OOEP, and WEE2

notes.statement: Jiao et al. (2025) recommended screening for MEI1 variants in patients with abnormal fertilization patterns, especially multiple pronuclei after ICSI. They noted that even embryos with apparently normal 2PN morphology may be triploid.
quotes: For clinical practice, we recommend MEI1 variant screening in patients showing abnormal fertilization patterns, especially multiple pronuclei following ICSI. In these cases, even embryos with apparently normal 2PN morphology may be triploid

notes.statement: Jiao et al. (2025) observed that MEI1 variants associated with nonobstructive azoospermia tended to lie toward the N terminus, while variants associated with embryonic developmental arrest tended to cluster toward the C terminus. They noted that this pattern requires further validation.
quotes: Interestingly, NOA-associated variants tend to locate towards the N-terminal, while EDA-related variants - including three novel variants identified in our study – tends to cluster toward the C-terminal.

notes.statement: In female patients from 2 unrelated families with primary infertility characterized by early embryonic arrest and implantation failure, Chen et al. (2026) identified a novel homozygous variant and compound heterozygous variants in the MEI1 gene by whole-exome sequencing, confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Bioinformatic analysis suggested the variants were rare and possibly deleterious.
quotes: Whole-exome sequencing was performed, and the identified variants were confirmed by Sanger sequencing.

We identified a novel homozygous variant and a compound heterozygous variant in MEI1 from two unrelated families. Analysis using multiple bioinformatics tools revealed that these variants are rare and may be deleterious.

notes.statement: In transfected HEK293T cells, Chen et al. (2026) found that the MEI1 variants did not alter subcellular localization of MEI1 but significantly affected its mRNA and protein expression levels, potentially impairing protein function.
quotes: In vitro experiments revealed that these mutations do not alter the subcellular localization of MEI1 but significantly affect its mRNA and protein expression levels, potentially leading to impaired protein function.

notes.statement: Liu et al. (2025) found by cDNA analysis that the homozygous MEI1 exon 19 deletion resulted in almost no detectable exon 19 expression, and Western blotting in transfected HEK293T cells showed production of a truncated MEI1 protein consistent with premature termination in exon 20. They described this as the first exon rearrangement reported in MEI1.
quotes: Quantitative expression revealed that the deletion result in almost no detectable expression of MEI1 Exon 19 in patients
Western blotting revealed that the whole exon deletion in MEI1 result in production of truncated MEI1 protein, corresponding to the predicted premature termination at Exon 20 of MEI1.
this study reported the first exon rearrangement of MEI1

notes.statement: Liu et al. (2025) found high rates of chromosomal anomalies on preimplantation genetic testing of arrested embryos from a woman with a homozygous MEI1 mutation, and suggested that embryonic aneuploidy may explain the reduced developmental potential and embryonic arrest.
quotes: Highly chromosomal anomalies were revealed in arrested embryos with MEI1 mutation.
revealed the aneuploidies of embryos with MEI1 mutation as a potential reason for declined developmental potency and embryonic arrest

notes.statement: Wu et al. (2024) found that 2 day-3 embryos and 2 day-6 blastocysts from a woman with MEI1 mutations were all aneuploid, with many monosomies and trisomies. Global methylation in the 2 blastocysts was 0.344 and 0.168, well outside the optimal window of 0.25 to 0.27. The authors suggested that the genetic makeup of arrested embryos from MEI1 patients gives clues about why some affected women have embryonic arrest and others have androgenetic hydatidiform moles.
quotes: Notably, two Day 3 embryos and two Day 6 blastocysts were all aneuploid, with numerous monosomy and trisomy events.
Moreover, global methylation levels greatly deviated from the optimized window of 0.25-0.27, measuring 0.344 and 0.168 for the respective blastocysts.
the genetic makeup of the arrested embryos of MEI1 patients provides important clues for understanding the different disease mechanisms of the two phenotypes.

notes.statement: Dong et al. (2021) used whole-exome sequencing with Sanger confirmation to identify 5 novel MEI1 mutations in 9 primary infertility patients from 7 families. They found that, in addition to recurrent hydatidiform moles, biallelic MEI1 mutations were associated with early embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure.
quotes: In this study, we identified five novel mutations in MEI1 in nine patients from seven independent families. Apart from recurrent hydatidiform moles, biallelic mutations in MEI1 were also associated with early embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure.
The MEI1 mutations were screened using whole-exome sequencing and were confirmed by the Sanger sequencing.

notes.statement: Dong et al. (2021) used in vitro western blotting to show that protein-truncating and missense MEI1 mutations reduced MEI1 protein levels. In minigene assays, the splicing mutations caused abnormal alternative splicing of MEI1. The authors noted that the exact mechanism remained unknown because no in vivo oocyte data were available.
quotes: In addition, we demonstrated that protein-truncating and missense mutations reduced the protein level of MEI1, while the splicing mutations caused abnormal alternative splicing of MEI1.
Owing to the lack of in vivo data from the oocytes of the patients, the exact molecular mechanism(s) involved in the phenotypes remains unknown
